questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

"Stop! Don't fight." said the mother to her children.

options.text: The mother exclaimed to her children angrily to stop and don't fight.
The mother exclaimed angrily to her children to stop and not fight.
The mother exclaimed to her children to pause and not engage in a fight.
The mother told her children to stop and not fight.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**The mother exclaimed angrily to her children to stop and not fight.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an example of **direct speech**, which means that it **reports someone else's words directly**.
 
• To convert **direct speech into indirect speech**, we need to follow certain rules, such as changing the **tense**, changing the **pronouns **and **adverbs**, and using **reporting verbs** like '**say', 'tell', 'exclaim', etc**.
 
• Let's apply these rules to the **given sentence**:
 
• The reported speech should convey the same message in indirect speech. So, the sentence can be written as, "**The mother instructed her children to stop and not fight**."
 
• We also need to add information about how the mother said this. In this case, she said it angrily. We can use the** reporting verb** '**exclaimed angrily**' to show the **tone** of the mother's words.
 
• The conjunction 'to' will be added and comma and inverted commas will be removed.
 
• The imperative sentence will be changed into an assertive sentence.
 
• According to the rules of grammar, after 'to' we have to use 'V1' (stop).
 
• So, the correct sentence in **indirect speech** is "**The mother exclaimed angrily to her children to stop and not fight**."
 
• Thus, ***option 2*** is the correct answer.

**Correct Indirect Speech:**__ *The mother exclaimed angrily to her children to stop and not fight.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Are fossil fuels not impacting human health?

options.text: Did human health not being impacted by fossil fuel?
Was human health not being impacted by fossil fuel?
Is human health not impacted by fossil fuel?
Is human health not being impacted by fossil fuel?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Is human health not being impacted by fossil fuel?**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The above given sentence is in active voice.
 
• We need to change it into passive voice.
 
• Let's look at the steps for changing it into passive voice:-
 
• The subject **'****fossil fuels**' becomes the object of the passive voice.
 
• The object **'human health' **becomes the subject of the passive voice.
 
• Since 'human health' is singular, therefore, 'is' has been used.
 
• The sentence is in present continuous tense. It will change according to the following structureZ:-
 
 
• Active Voice - is/am/are + Ving
 
• Passive voice - is/am/are + being + V3
 
 
 
• For Example:-
 
 
• Active Voice - Is the lyricist **writing **realistic songs?
 
• Passive Voice - Are realistic songs **being written **by the lyricist.
 
 
 
• **'not impacting' **changes to** 'not being impacted'**.
 
• Thus, **option 4** is the correct answer.

**Correct Passive Voice:**__ *Is human health not being impacted by fossil fuel?*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

__Reading has the capacity to make a man wise,__ but reading of only textbooks is like living in room of our same height.

options.text: Reading should make a man wise
Reading shall make a man wise

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Reading makes a man wise**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is: "**Reading has the capacity to make a man wise**."
 
• This option correctly conveys the intended meaning of the original sentence that **reading has the potential or ability to make a person wise**.
 
• **Option 2** is incorrect as it does not use the correct **subject-verb agreement** (**make should be changed to makes to agree with the singular subject "Reading"**).
 
• **Option 3 and 4 **are also incorrect as they suggest an **obligation **or a **certainty **that reading will make a man wise, which is not necessarily true.
 
• The original sentence is suggesting that reading has the potential to make a person wise, but that potential is limited if one only reads textbooks, like living in a room of the same height, implying that one needs to read more broadly to truly gain wisdom.
 
• Thus, ***option 1*** is the correct answer.

**Correct Sentence:**__ *__**Reading makes a man wise**__, but reading of only textbooks is like living in room of our same height. *
